edits.name: Saved notes: 'remember this' goes to that parent's own notes and is found again by keyword
edits.description: A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent saves the line to that parent's own notes and says what it saved. edits.example: A parent texts: 'Remember that the library books are due back on the 20th.' A week later, in a new chat, the same parent asks 'when are the library books due?' and Happy finds the note and answers. The other parent's agent cannot find it.
edits.how: T6 runs first, on Tony's eval-only copy, before any setting changes. Then the generator gives the parent's agent `write` and `edit` (also in the sandbox tool gate) with `apply_patch` denied by name, and `memory_search` and `memory_get`, keyword-only (`memory.search.provider: "none"`, already set). The sandbox stays closed to the agent folder (`workspaceAccess: "none"`), so a note is written to a notes folder inside the agent's own sandbox workspace, and that folder is added to that agent's own `memory.search.extraPaths` (per agent, never global). One instruction: save only what the parent asked to save, in the parent's words, and say what was saved. House-rules plugin: at most one rule, 'notes may be written only inside the notes folder', added only if T6 leaves a need for it. Not built: a read-write workspace, tracking of web tool calls, the session-memory hook, any copy of notes outside the agent. The separation canaries are extended to memory search. Tony's agent first.

edits.name: Read-only Gmail: a weekday morning mail text, school lines first; asking about a mail on Tony's yes
edits.description: Each parent approves read-only access to their own Gmail once on Google's own screen; the token stays on the Mac mini, Happy never holds a password, and nothing in Gmail is changed, drafted or sent. Each weekday at 07:00 a locked-down mail reader texts its owner a short list of what needs a reply, has a deadline or involves money, school lines first and without links; it starts with Tony's inbox, and Jordan's is added when she says yes. If Tony says yes to it, a parent can also ask 'did I get an email about X?' and get the sender, the date and the gist.
edits.example: 07:00, text to Tony: 'School: a notice about an early closing on Friday 16 October. Needs you: the plumber asks you to confirm Thursday's visit by tomorrow; a bill is due on Tuesday 20 October. Nothing else needs a reply.' If the lookup is switched on, Tony texts 'did the plumber confirm Thursday?' and gets the sender, the date and one line of gist from his own inbox.
edits.how:
Connector: gog's own MCP server (`gog mcp`), a host-side stdio entry under `mcp.servers`, started with only its owner's token and narrowed with `--allow-tool` to the Gmail read tools; one read-only token per inbox from `gog auth add` (`--services` limited to Gmail, `--gmail-scope readonly`). Reader: one `

-mail` agent per connected inbox, generated from the family file: `profile: "minimal"`, only `

-gmail__*` allowed (also in `tools.sandbox.tools`), denied by name on every other agent; no other tool; memory search off; one cloud model, storage off, no fallback. Firewall: one rule, the connector reaches Google only. Digest: one weekday 07:00 job from the jobs script, Gmail read tools only, delivered to its owner: school lines first, no links, medical mail by sender and subject only. Lookup, on Tony's yes: `

-main` hands the question to its own `

-mail` through `subagents.allowAgents`, with a time limit. House-rules plugin: no rule now; the account-connector rule is added when the plugin is first created.

Mail text goes to the cloud model on Tony's go-ahead of 12 Oct. Until OpenAI approves Zero Data Retention its abuse-monitoring log can keep that text for up to 30 days, and reading mail on a cloud model departs from the roadmap's rule of a local model for mail readers.

If the day-8 search fails, the choice is a weekly sign-in or a different connector.

'No links' and 'sender and subject only for medical mail' are instructions to the reader, not enforced limits. What limits harm is that the reader holds only Gmail read tools and its one output is the scheduled text to its owner.
Google's Gemini app already answers questions from a person's own Gmail and lists a daily digest among its scheduled actions; Happy adds only asking, and being told, in the iMessage thread.

The lookup goes one step beyond the roadmap's mail design: its answer comes back into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's chat history and, after wave B, can hand a task to the web helper. Only a prompt rule and seeded tests stand between them, so it is built only on Tony's yes and can stay off.
edits.safety: The reader holds private mail and reads outsiders' text, so it gets no way out: no web, file, code, browser, draft, send or message tool, and its one output is the scheduled text to its owner. Until the house-rules plugin exists, who may call the connector rests on tool permissions, an explicit deny and two tests. The lookup, if built, is the weaker half.
